summary: Graves Mountain, WA: 1934 pole tower and cabin, replaced in 1955 by an L-4 cab; the cab was moved to Colville in 1985 and restored, and the mountain site has no tower.

facts.design: Original 1934 pole tower of 72 feet with an accompanying log cabin for living quarters; 1955 replacement 30-foot timber tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Tower removed from Graves Mountain in 1985 and moved to Colville; the sources read do not describe what remains on the mountain today
facts.agency: Stevens County Historical Society (administers the restored cab); U.S. Forest Service built and replaced the lookout

access.note: Restored cab in Colville: register says open to the public daily; firelookout.com says open for summer tours; a regional listing gives the museum season as May 1 to September 30. Mountain site has no tower and no access described.

events.note: 72-foot pole tower with log cabin built on the mountain by the Forest Service and CCC; the historical society says early 1930s
Pole tower replaced by a 30-foot timber tower with an L-4 cab
First year in the firelookout.com personnel list; the list does not say when staffing ended
Stevens County Historical Society moved the tower and cab, piece by piece, to Colville; the tower was removed from the mountain
Mountain site registered November 17, 2012 as US 1449, WA 349

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firetower.org give 72 feet, Willhite says 72 feet (possibly 80), and the historical society says 75 feet. The story reports the disagreement; facts use the 30-foot 1955 tower that stood on the mountain until 1985.
Register says the L-4 cab stood 30 years; the historical society says the station functioned for almost 50 years. Both are reported.

Register says open to the public daily; firelookout.com says open for tours during the summer; a regional events listing gives a May 1 to September 30 museum season. Reported as conflicting, with no climbing rule found.
Register gives 5,901 ft (1,799 m); firetower.org and the historical society give 5,947 ft (1,813 m) for the mountain site. The record keeps the register value.

notes_for_editor: Covers the 1934-1985 mountain site and the move to Colville; the museum record us-wa-graves-mountain-at-colville-museum shares most of these sources. Height (72 vs 75 ft) and museum access are disputed across sources and reported as such. No staffing end date or notable fires were found. Lookout names from the 1955-1959 personnel lists are left out, as in the museum record. The NHLR register's Stevens County Park and Museum and the Keller Historical Museum may be the same site; the sources do not confirm it. Not read: Visit Northeast Washington social posts that the sibling record mentions. Museum season is from a regional event listing, not the museum's own site.
